function: Optimizes device equalization, receive beamforming, shared RIS phases and downlink beamforming for minimum-latency covert over-the-air FL aggregation by alternating optimization; no learned physical-layer component (pp. 1, 3-4).
system: J=5-antenna BS, M=8 single-antenna devices, single-antenna warden, reflecting RIS with L=36 elements (ULA); 2 MHz bandwidth, carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2, 5).
method: Federated learning with over-the-air model aggregation (system model only, no training run); physical-layer design by alternating optimization with SDR, SCA and bisection (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Own simulated channels: large-scale path loss with exponents 3.8, 2.2, 2.2, 3.5 and 2.3, small-scale Rayleigh fading; no standard model, dataset or measurement (p. 5).
test_conditions: No trained model; one layout (BS, RIS, warden fixed, 8 devices random); Fig. 1 sweeps covertness level, RIS elements 16-64 and BS antennas 3-7 (p. 5).
baselines: No RIS (NR); MSE minimization at BS with RIS [6] (MR); separate uplink and downlink RIS design with SDR (FK, no citation). All optimization-based (p. 5).
metrics: Communication latency (delay in seconds) versus iterations, covertness level, RIS elements and BS antennas (Fig. 1, p. 5).
complexity: Worst-case complexity expression of the alternating-optimization framework, footnote 3 (p. 5), with terms like [(J+1)^2]^3, M^3 and [(L+1)^2+M]^3 per AO iteration.
q1_support: p. 5: "small-scale Rayleigh fading" with path-loss exponents 3.8, 2.2, 2.2, 3.5 and 2.3 is the own simulated channel; no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 5: "we evaluate the communication latency with different numbers" of BS antennas (also RIS elements and covertness level) re-solves the optimization for each setting; no trained model is tested on unseen conditions.
q3_support: p. 5: "Minimizing MSE at BS with RIS (MR) [6]" is an earlier published over-the-air aggregation design (FL via IRS) and NR is the no-RIS case; both are compared with OPT on latency in Fig. 1 (delay in seconds). Met under the over-the-air FL rule; FK is a variant without citation.
q4_support: p. 5: "the worst-case complexity of the AO framework" is given in footnote 3 as t_max(C_F + C_P + C_X + D(L+1)^2 + [(J)^2]^3) with C_F, C_P and C_X defined there; it is the cost of the RIS and transceiver design, so it counts.
q5_support: p. 4: "We consider the following simulation setup in this letter" with own parameters (continued on p. 5); no code or data link, no public dataset or measured data and no availability statement appear on pp. 1-5.
notes: Included only through the Step 1.3 rule for FL over the air: the physical-layer design is classical optimization (AO, SDR, SCA, bisection) and no FL training or accuracy is simulated, so the reviewer should confirm eligibility. Area 7 because the over-the-air aggregation with RIS is the problem solved. q3 follows the FL over the air rule (MR [6] is an earlier aggregation design). In Fig. 1 the FK baseline shows lower delay than the proposed OPT; the text attributes it to higher complexity (p. 5).
